[EFFECT] The year feature acts as a simple on/off switch: hours in 2011 (yr = 0) consistently pull predicted demand **down** (negative contributions around –0.30 on average), while hours in 2012 (yr = 1) push it **up** (positive contributions around +0.17 on average). This is a sharp step change with no gradual transition — the model sees 2012 as a fundamentally higher-demand environment than 2011. The peak contribution belongs entirely to 2012.

[IMPORTANCE] Year is the **second most important** feature out of the nine used by the model, with an importance score of 0.20. Only one other feature influences demand more strongly, meaning the year alone accounts for a large share of the model's predictions.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because 2012 showed systematically higher demand than 2011, any future year-over-year growth should be explicitly accounted for in your staffing and fleet-size planning — do not assume demand levels from an earlier year are a reliable baseline for the next.
